51602445.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human recombinant PLA2 receptor assessed as dissociation constant by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - 2.3. Surface pla: Multicycle kinetics affinities between immobilized PLA2R and purified anti-PLA2R IgG were assessed on the BIAcore 8 K system (GE Healthcare, USA). Multicycle kinetics affinities between compounds and proteins were performed on BIAcore 200 platform (GE Healthcare, USA). CM5 chip was activated by EDC/NHS. Purified recombinant PLA2R proteins, ranging from 20 to 50 μg/mL and diluted in 10 mM sodium acetate at a pH of 4.5, were immobilized on the chip using standard amine coupling chemistry. Sensors were then deactivated by ethanolamine to prevent further immobilization of proteins. Multicycle kinetic runs were performed using eight concentrations of anti-PLA2R antibody in HEPES buffer (pH 7.2) containing 0.005 % Tween 20. Each injection lasted for 180 s at a flow rate of 30 μL/m with a 600-second dissociation phase. Sensor regeneration was achieved by a 30-second wash in 100 mM glycine at pH 1.5. All samples were referenced with the blank row. Data analysis involved fitting the results to a Langmuir 1:1 interaction model. All experiments were performed at least three times.
original_paragraph.Results - 3.1. The binding affinity of a: We assessed the affinity of human anti-PLA2R IgG, purified from three patients with PLA2R-associated MN before any immunosuppressive therapy, for binding to the full-length extracellular PLA2R protein. The antibody affinity demonstrated consistency among the patients. The calculated dissociation constant (Kd) values were as follows: 2.1 × 10⁻⁸ M for patient 1 with an anti-PLA2R level of 143RU/mL, 7.4 × 10⁻⁸ M for patient 2 with an anti-PLA2R level of 208RU/mL, and 2.1 × 10⁻⁸ M for patient 3 with an anti-PLA2R level of 147RU/mL, respectively (Fig. 1).
original_paragraph.Figure 1 caption: Fig. 1. Affinity of anti-PLA2R IgG from MN patients. The affinity of anti-PLA2R IgG from the patients with PLA2R-associated MN was tested against immobilized PLA2R using surface plasmon resonance (SPR). (A) patient 1 possessed anti-PLA2R antibodies at a level of 143RU/mL. (B) patient 2 had anti-PLA2R antibodies of 208RU/mL. (C) patient 3 had anti-PLA2R antibodies of 147RU/mL.
original_paragraph.Results - 3.4. Binding between the inhib: To further elucidate the interaction among PLA2R, Macrocarpal B, and anti-PLA2R IgG, we conducted a compound-protein binding assay using SPR. Macrocarpal B was flowed over immobilized PLA2R or anti-PLA2R IgG, separately. The assay results demonstrated that Macrocarpal B is bound to immobilized PLA2R with an affinity of approximately 1.47 × 10⁻⁶ M (Fig. 3A). Conversely, no interaction was observed between Macrocarpal B and anti-PLA2R IgG (Fig. 3B-D).
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Fig. 3. Binding assay of Macrocarpal B with PLA2R and anti-PLA2R IgG. Sensorgrams were obtained from injections of Macrocarpal B at varying concentrations over immobilized proteins (PLA2R or anti-PLA2R IgG) using SPR. Macrocarpal B demonstrated an affinity for PLA2R with a dissociation constant (Kd) of 1.47 × 10⁻⁶ M(A). Kinetic constants were unattainable for the interaction between Macrocarpal B and anti-PLA2R IgG from patient 1 (B), patient 2 (C), and patient 3 (D) due to low response and poor fitting of the sensorgrams in the multicycle analysis.
original_paragraph.Discussion: Macrocarpal B exhibited binding to immobilized PLA2R with a dissociation constant (Kd) of 10⁻⁶ M, which was much weaker than that of anti-PLA2R IgG, with a Kd of 10⁻⁸ M. Despite this weaker affinity, Macrocarpal B was still capable of inhibiting the interaction between PLA2R and its antibodies.

analyte.description: anti-PLA2R IgG (from patients) and Macrocarpal B
analyte.concentration_range: anti-PLA2R IgG: 8 concentrations in HEPES buffer; Macrocarpal B: 0.39μM to 200μM (Panel A), 1μM to 125μM (Panels B-C), 3.9μM to 500μM (Panel D)
